sections.title: Storm damage inspection and repair in Mission
paras: After a hailstorm or high wind event, roof damage isn't always obvious from the ground. Missing granules, bruised shingles, and lifted flashing can go unnoticed for months until they turn into a leak. We inspect the whole roof, not just the parts you can see from your driveway, and tell you honestly what we find.

If the damage is real, we document it in writing with enough detail to support an insurance claim. If it's cosmetic and doesn't affect the roof's performance, we tell you that too. We're not paid more for finding damage that isn't there.

sections.title: What a storm damage inspection covers

cards.title: Hail Impact
cards.body: Bruising, granule loss, and cracked shingles from hail impact. We check the whole roof, not just the sides that face the street.

cards.title: Wind Uplift & Missing Shingles
cards.body: High wind can lift or tear shingles even when nothing looks obviously wrong from below. We check every edge, ridge, and valley.

cards.title: Flashing & Vent Damage
cards.body: Storms move flashing and knock loose the seals around vents and skylights, a common source of leaks that shows up weeks later.

cards.title: Written Insurance Documentation
cards.body: Photos and a written report of exactly what we found, useful when you file a claim. We're not a public adjuster, but we'll walk you through what we observed.

sections.title: Storm damage we see in Mission
paras: Older homes around Conway Avenue and the streets running toward downtown have shingle roofs that have already been through a lot of Valley summers. A hailstorm that only scuffs a newer roof can be the last straw on one of those, and we say so plainly during the inspection.

In Sharyland and the newer subdivisions west and north of town, the roofs are younger, so storm damage tends to be specific: a run of lifted shingles, a loose vent seal, bent flashing. Those are often repairs, not replacements.

On the commercial side, the retail along Expressway 83 and the buildings near Mission Regional Medical Center mostly have flat or low slope roofs. Wind can peel a membrane at the edges, and after a heavy rain water pools where it shouldn't. That takes a different kind of inspection than a pitched roof.

faqs.q: How do I know if I have hail damage on my roof?
faqs.a: Hail damage often isn't visible from the ground, bruised shingles and granule loss show up close-up, not from your driveway. If there was a hailstorm in your area, it's worth getting a free inspection even if nothing looks wrong yet.

faqs.q: Do you help with insurance claims for storm damage?
faqs.a: We inspect the roof and give you a written report with photos documenting what we find. That documentation is useful when you file a claim. We're not a public adjuster, but we'll walk you through what we observed so you know what to present to your insurer.

faqs.q: How soon should I get an inspection after a storm?
faqs.a: Sooner is better. Some insurance policies have a filing window after a storm event, and damage that isn't causing a leak yet can worsen with the next rain. A free inspection costs you nothing either way.

faqs.q: Does storm damage always mean I need a full roof replacement?
faqs.a: No. Sometimes it's a targeted repair, a few shingles, some flashing, a resealed vent. We recommend replacement only when the damage or the roof's age actually calls for it, not by default.

faqs.q: How do I get a storm damage inspection in Mission?
faqs.a: Call us at (956) 422-3335 or book online. We'll inspect the roof, document what we find, and give you a written estimate if repair or replacement is needed. Inspections are free with no obligation.
